metadata.title: From Prediction to Explanation: Integrating Ensemble Machine Learning and Structural Equation Modeling in Reading Literacy
metadata.venue: Eğitimde ve Psikolojide Ölçme ve Değerlendirme Dergisi (Journal of Measurement and Evaluation in Education and Psychology)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PIRLS 2021 student questionnaire and reading comprehension plausible values for Finland, Portugal, and Türkiye, with an analytic sample formed after excluding observations with extensive missingness (more than 70% missing across 12 predictors) and removing cases responsible for specific missingness patterns among key variables. Missing values were then imputed using missForest, and the authors report checking distributional similarity before vs. after imputation and assessing multicollinearity via VIF (all below 10). For the machine-learning stage, student weights were incorporated during both hyperparameter tuning and model building, and the same weighted approach was used in SEM estimation. The manuscript does not report replicate-weight methodology (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so uncertainty estimation is described via bootstrap resampling in SEM rather than replicate-weight procedures.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PIRLS 2021 fourth-grade student data for Finland, Portugal, and Türkiye. Excluded observations with missing values in more than 70% (eight or more) of the 12 predictors used. Additionally, identified missingness patterns where specific sets of variables were missing together (parents’ perceptions of child’s school, early literacy tasks, home learning resources, parents like reading, and preschool attendance) and excluded the observations responsible for these patterns (Finland: 434 cases; Portugal: 171 cases; Türkiye: 428 cases). After exclusions, imputed remaining missing values using missForest and proceeded with ML (separate 70/30 gender-stratified train/test splits) and SEM on the full datasets.

main_findings.dataset_used: PIRLS 2021 Grade 4 Reading comprehension (Finland, Portugal, Türkiye)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Bagging vs Random Forest vs Gradient Boosting (per country): Finland R²≈0.32–0.34, RMSE≈58.9–59.6, MAE≈46.4–47.1; Portugal R²≈0.37–0.38, RMSE≈54.8–55.6, MAE≈43.3–44.0; Türkiye R²≈0.37–0.40, RMSE≈65.9–67.4, MAE≈51.9–52.9. Variable importance rankings were consistent across algorithms within each country; gradient boosting used for partial dependence plots.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PIRLS 2021 Grade 4 reading comprehension plausible values data for Finland, Portugal, and Türkiye, the study leveraged reading confidence, early literacy tasks, and home learning resources (with related motivation/home-attitude variables) to predict reading comprehension achievement, finding that all three ensemble algorithms achieved similar moderate predictive performance across countries and that variable-importance rankings were highly consistent within each country. This indicates that combining ensemble ML with interpretable importance measures can reliably identify stable, context-sensitive correlates of reading literacy for targeting interventions, though the study’s causal claims rely on SEM rather than ML prediction alone.

main_findings.dataset_used: PIRLS 2021 Grade 4 Reading comprehension (SEM models by country)
main_findings.performance_metrics: SEM fit: Finland CFI=0.979, RMSEA=0.072, SRMR=0.025; Portugal CFI=0.964, RMSEA=0.075, SRMR=0.035; Türkiye CFI=0.976, RMSEA=0.068, SRMR=0.030. Total effects (p<.01): Finland Early_lit_task=0.327, Home_res_learn=0.271; Portugal Home_res_learn=0.382, Reading confidence=0.384; Türkiye Home_res_learn=0.477, Reading confidence=0.307.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PIRLS 2021 Grade 4 reading literacy (READ1) the study leveraged home learning resources, early literacy tasks, and reading confidence (selected from ML variable-importance outputs) to estimate direct and indirect structural effects via SEM, finding that home and parental factors were more prominent in Türkiye, student confidence was dominant in Portugal, and early literacy tasks had a noteworthy impact in Finland. This indicates that policy should be tailored by context—e.g., strengthening home learning resources may be especially important where home-based inequalities are larger, while confidence-building and early literacy supports may yield greater returns in higher-achieving systems—while recognizing that SEM supports hypothesized pathways rather than proving untestable causal assumptions.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PIRLS 2021 Grade 4 reading comprehension for Finland (n=6,556), Portugal (n=5,934), and Türkiye (n=5,594), using plausible values as the dependent outcome. Three ensemble ML methods—bagging, random forests, and gradient boosting—show similar moderate predictive performance across countries, with R² around 0.32–0.40 and RMSE roughly 55–67 depending on country; variable-importance rankings were consistent within each country. The authors then use SEM to test structural relationships among the most influential predictors identified by ML, reporting good model fit (CFI≈0.964–0.979; RMSEA≈0.068–0.075; SRMR≈0.025–0.035). Key structural patterns differ by context: early literacy tasks are strongest in Finland, reading confidence is dominant in Portugal, and home learning resources are strongest in Türkiye. Limitations include reliance on SEM for causal interpretation (not ML), and the paper does not report replicate-weight procedures, while ML performance is based on train/test splits with gender stratification and hyperparameter tuning via grid search.
